g.text: Spawning: about 1 h 53 after sunset, every night
Each dot: one coral genus starting to spawn on one night
Before full moon, the Moon is already up at sunset
The Moon reaches the spawning hour. From the next night, that hour is dark.

polygon.style: stroke-width: 1.07; stroke: none; stroke-linecap: butt; fill: #1F3549;
stroke-width: 1.07; stroke: none; stroke-linecap: butt; fill: #F1EAD7;

g.text: Moon at moonrise, in that night’s phase

rect.style: stroke-width: 0.64; stroke: #31475A;

g.text: Each row is one evening. The Moon rises later every night, but corals keep their hour.
They peak on nights +3 to +6 (62% of starts), the first evenings when that hour is dark.
The Sun fixes the hour, the Moon decides when it goes dark
A pattern, not proof of a trigger: people also chose which nights to watch. At the same reefs and clock times the Moon is down for 76% of starts, against 50% on the 28 surrounding dates.

316 of 327 timed starts shown, 35 reef sites. Sky and moonrise: typical values across those reefs. Same-reef trend, approximate times included: +1.7 min per night (95% CI 0.5 to 3.4). Data: Baird et al. (2021).
